subject.title: Config: scaffold compaction loop guard settings

question: Should OpenClaw reserve a new `agents.defaults.compaction.guard` config surface, or should any remaining loop-guard behavior use the existing `tools.loopDetection.postCompactionGuard` and the canonical saturated-session design issue?
rationale: This is a public config/default direction, not a mechanical repair: it affects upgrade semantics, docs, and which namespace users will rely on for compaction-loop protection.

options.title: Use The Existing Guard Namespace
options.body: Rework the PR so any remaining behavior extends `tools.loopDetection.postCompactionGuard` or a maintainer-approved follow-up, avoiding a no-op parallel config block.

options.title: Sponsor The New Compaction Guard Surface
options.body: Keep the new namespace only if maintainers explicitly want `agents.defaults.compaction.guard` as a future public contract and define its runtime relationship to the existing guard.

options.title: Close Or Replace This Branch
options.body: Treat this stale conflicting scaffold as superseded and ask for a fresh narrow PR after the design issue is resolved.

recommendation.title: Use The Existing Guard Namespace
recommendation.body: Rework the PR so any remaining behavior extends `tools.loopDetection.postCompactionGuard` or a maintainer-approved follow-up, avoiding a no-op parallel config block.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete merged and authored recent post-compaction guard follow-ups and is the clearest current owner for the config/runtime namespace decision.
